pages.title: Consultations
pages.content:
Not sure which service you need? Book a free fifteen-minute consultation and we will look at your hair together, talk through options and give you a written quote.

Colour consultations

Bring a few photos of looks you like, and one or two you don't. We will talk about upkeep honestly: a soft balayage can grow out gracefully for four months, while a bright copper wants a gloss every five weeks.

Bridal trials

Trials take ninety minutes and include a written plan for the day, so whoever does your hair on the morning knows exactly which pins go where.

Request a consultation

pages.title: About the salon
pages.content:
A salon that takes its time

Velvet opened in a former milliner's workshop in 2014 with two chairs and a borrowed hood dryer. Today there are eight of us, but the idea has stayed the same: book fewer clients, spend longer with each one, and send everybody home with hair they understand.

We work with low-ammonia colour, refill our shampoos from bulk containers and send our hair clippings to a scheme that turns them into oil-spill booms. Small things, done every day.

The team

Meet the stylists

Ines

Founder · Colour director

Fifteen years of balayage and a soft spot for copper. Ines trains every new colourist herself.

Maren

Senior stylist · Bridal

Maren has pinned more than four hundred wedding up-dos and has never lost a veil.

Teo

Stylist · Short cuts

Clipper work, textured crops and the sharpest fringe in the arcade. Ask about curl cuts.

I wanted a salon where nobody is rushed, including the stylist. That is still the whole plan.

Ines, founder

pages.title: Book an appointment
pages.content:
We take bookings by phone and in the salon, and we keep a few same-week slots for colour corrections and last-minute events.

New clients

Tell us what you are hoping for and how much time you have. First colours need a quick skin test 48 hours ahead.

Returning clients

Ask for your usual stylist; we keep notes on your formula and finish so you never have to explain twice.

Groups & weddings

Up to six people at once on Saturdays. We will plan the timings so the bride is finished last and freshest.

Call +1 (555) 014-2290 between 9 am and 7 pm, Tuesday to Saturday, or drop in and we will find a time together.

posts.title: How to make a blow-dry last until Friday
posts.excerpt: Five small habits that keep a Monday blow-dry bouncy all week, from the pillowcase to the dry shampoo trick.
posts.content:
A good blow-dry should not be a one-day treat. With a few habits, the volume and smoothness you leave the salon with on Monday can still be there on Friday, give or take a little touch-up.

Start on the first night

Before bed, loosely twist your hair into a high, soft bun on the crown and secure it with a fabric scrunchie. It keeps the roots lifted and stops the ends from being crushed into the pillow.

  • Swap to a silk or satin pillowcase; cotton grabs at the cuticle.
  • Skip heavy night creams along the hairline.
  • Keep a shower cap by the bath and use it every time.

Dry shampoo before you need it

The trick most people miss is timing. Spray dry shampoo at the roots on the second evening, before your hair feels greasy, and brush it through in the morning. It absorbs oil overnight instead of fighting it.

Treat day two as maintenance, not rescue. It is much easier to keep volume than to bring it back.

Maren, senior stylist

A two-minute refresh

By day four, rough-dry just the front sections with a round brush and a cool shot. Everything behind the ears can stay as it is; nobody looks there as closely as you do.

comments.author: Lotte
comments.content: The bun-before-bed trick has changed my life. Day five and still bouncy!

comments.author: Maren
comments.content: So glad it worked! Try the cool shot on the fringe too next time.

posts.title: Balayage or highlights? How to choose
posts.excerpt: Both brighten your hair, but they grow out very differently. Here is how we help clients decide.
posts.content:
It is the question we hear most at the colour bar, usually with a phone full of photos. Both techniques add brightness, but they behave very differently once you leave the salon.

Balayage

  • Painted by hand, softer at the roots
  • Grows out gently over three to four months
  • Best for natural, sun-touched brightness

Foil highlights

  • Precise, even lightness from the root
  • Needs a refresh every eight to ten weeks
  • Best for brighter blondes and grey blending

If you like low upkeep and do not mind a darker root, balayage is usually the answer. If you want to look noticeably blonder, or you are covering grey, foils give a cleaner result.

Many of our clients end up with a mix of the two: a few fine foils around the parting and face, with balayage through the lengths. Ask for a free consultation and we will plan it together.

comments.author: Priya
comments.content: I went for the mix after my consultation with Ines and I love how soft the regrowth is.

posts.title: Five colours we are mixing this autumn
posts.excerpt: Cinnamon, smoky plum and soft mushroom blonde: the shades our colourists are mixing most as the evenings draw in.
posts.content:
Every September the colour bar changes. Lighter summer blondes come in asking for depth, and the copper bowls come out of the cupboard. These are the five shades we have mixed most so far.

  1. Cinnamon copper: warm, soft and kind to freckles.
  2. Smoky plum: a violet-brown that only shows in the light.
  3. Mushroom blonde: an ashy beige that tones down brassiness.
  4. Espresso gloss: rich, reflective brunette with no bands.
  5. Rose gold melt: a pastel pink fading into blonde ends.

Darker, glossier shades are also kinder to hair after a summer of sun and salt. A gloss seals the cuticle, so your hair reflects more light and feels softer.

Not sure which shade suits you? Hold a swatch against your jaw in daylight by the window at reception; your skin will tell you more than any photo can.

posts.title: A gentle routine for a healthy scalp
posts.excerpt: Good hair starts at the root. A weekly routine that calms itchiness, flakes and oily roots without harsh products.
posts.content:
A healthy scalp is the foundation of every good haircut, yet it is the part of our hair routine we think about least. Itchiness, flaking and oily roots are often signs that the scalp needs a reset, not stronger products.

Once a week

  • Brush dry hair from the roots with a boar or wide paddle brush to lift product build-up.
  • Massage a few drops of a light oil into the scalp for five minutes.
  • Wash twice: the first wash removes oil, the second actually cleans.

Every wash

Use lukewarm water, not hot, and work shampoo into the scalp with your fingertips rather than your nails. Conditioner belongs on the lengths and ends only; keeping it off the scalp stops roots from going flat.

If flaking continues for more than a few weeks, mention it at your next visit; we will suggest a treatment or let you know when it is worth seeing a doctor.

posts.title: Your first lash lift: what to expect
posts.excerpt: Fifty minutes with your eyes closed and six weeks of curl. Everything you need to know before booking a lash lift.
posts.content:
A lash lift curls your natural lashes from the root, so they look longer and more open without extensions or mascara. It is one of the most relaxing treatments we offer: you lie back with your eyes closed for most of it.

How it works

  1. We clean the lashes and fit a soft silicone shield to the lid.
  2. Each lash is combed up over the shield and set with a gentle lotion.
  3. A tint adds depth, then everything is cleaned away.

Afterwards, keep your lashes dry for 24 hours and skip the sauna. From then on you can wash, swim and sleep as normal, and the curl will last six to eight weeks.

Most clients fall asleep. That is how we know we got the pillow right.

Our beauty therapist

Lash lifts are not suitable during an eye infection or within a few weeks of eye surgery. If in doubt, book a free patch test and ask us anything.

posts.title: Welcome Teo, our new short-hair specialist
posts.excerpt: Clipper fades, textured crops and curl cuts: meet the newest stylist at Velvet.
posts.content:
We are delighted to welcome Teo to the salon. Teo joins us from a busy barbershop across the river and brings sharp clipper skills, a calm manner and a playlist that is already a favourite at the back basins.

Teo specialises in short cuts of every kind, from soft pixies to skin fades, and is training with Ines in curl cutting, where hair is cut dry, curl by curl, to respect its natural shape.

Introductory offer

Throughout September, book a short cut with Teo and the fringe trims in between are on us. Mention this post when you call.

comments.author: Jonah
comments.content: Had my first cut with Teo last week. Best fade I have had in years.

posts.title: A calm wedding-morning hair timeline
posts.excerpt: How we plan hair for a bride and five guests without anyone watching the clock.
posts.content:
A wedding morning should feel like a slow breakfast with friends, not a race. After hundreds of bridal parties, Maren has a timeline that keeps everyone calm and the bride's hair at its freshest for the photographs.

A sample morning for six

We always finish the bride last, and we leave thirty minutes free before the car arrives. That half hour is the secret: it absorbs late arrivals, spilled coffee and the inevitable second thoughts about the fringe.

Before the day

Book a trial six to eight weeks before the day. Bring your veil or hair accessories, and wear a top with a similar neckline to your dress.
